title: RBACv2 validation gates and admin-edge safeguards migration playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create and execute a migration playbook that moves customers from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with minimal service disruption. The work focuses on staged verification gates, admin-edge feature toggles, audit-preservation, SSO/SAML mapping validation, and a safe fallback/rollback path. This ticket covers the validator design, runbook automation, observability checks, and customer-facing comms drafts for enterprise tenants with strict audit requirements.
acceptance_criteria: All staged validation gates implemented and automated in CI for canary waves
Admin-edge feature toggles allow opt-out for 48 hours post-wave without data loss
Audit logs for role changes are captured and exportable in both v1 and v2 formats for 90 days
SSO/SAML mapping smoke tests pass for top 10 enterprise customers (synthetic run)
Rollback path validated end-to-end with no permanent loss of role bindings
Customer communications templates reviewed by Legal and Product and ready for scheduled sends
rollout_steps: 1) Feature-flagged dual-write enabled for role updates (v1->v2) on dev environment
2) Run automated reconciliation job to compare authoritative role-store outputs for 48h
3) Canary Wave A (internal accounts): enable validator gates + observability dashboards
4) Canary Wave B (non-critical external customers): enable dual-write and collect telemetry
5) Wave-by-wave onboarding: increase customer cohort by 5x after passing validation thresholds
6) Final cutover window: flip read path to RBAC v2 while keeping v1 write-mirroring for 72h
7) Post-cutover reconciliation: run full backfill and generate audit delta report for compliance team
rollback_plan: If validator gates detect >0.5% authorization error rate or any high-severity audit mismatch, immediately disable RBACv2 read path and revert to v1 reads. Maintain v2 write-mirroring so no new role data is lost. Run automated reconciliation and a synthetic verification suite before attempting re-enable. Escalation to on-call security engineer and product manager required for approval to continue.
observability_checks: End-to-end latency delta between v1 and v2 for common APIs (authz check, role enumeration)
Audit log parity check: events emitted to audit service from both v1 and v2 for same action
KV cache hit ratios and cache-miss-induced auth latency spikes
SSO assertion failure rate by IdP and mapping error categories

customer_communications_draft:
Subject: Upcoming RBAC migration window (what to expect)

Hello,

We are moving to RBAC v2 to improve admin controls, audit fidelity, and SSO mapping resilience. This change will be rolled out in staged waves. During your customer's wave we will first run non-invasive validations and only enable enforcement after successful verification. No immediate action is required from you unless you receive a request from your admin console to confirm role mappings. If you have a custom SSO/SAML mapping, we will contact your technical owner to validate assertions.

Planned maintenance window: UTC nights (low-traffic) over the scheduled wave. For enterprise customers requiring a private cutover time, reply to this message to coordinate.

- Redwood Security Team
risk_assessment: Risk: SAML mapping mismatch for customers using custom attribute transforms -> Likelihood: Medium; Impact: High
Mitigation: Pre-run SAML assertion simulator and schedule mapping review calls with top-10 affected customers
Risk: Audit log divergence causing compliance reports to fail -> Likelihood: Low; Impact: High
Mitigation: Emit parallel audit events and provide delta reports to compliance for 90-day overlap
Risk: Increased auth latency due to initial cache cold-start -> Likelihood: High; Impact: Medium
Mitigation: Warm caches via synthetic traffic and gradual ramping of rollout cohorts
notes: This playbook intentionally keeps RBACv1 as a writable fallback for 72 hours post-cutover to eliminate irreversible state loss. We are coordinating with Console team to surface a per-tenant 'migration health' widget and with Support to prepare runbooks for customer calls.
